Specify persistent fertility weights and maternal inheritance

Source: R/het_fert.R
het_fert.Rd

Weights redistribute births among eligible women within a fertility cell; they do not multiply the cell's target rate. Fresh weights are lognormal with mean one and coefficient of variation cv. Daughters inherit on the normal scale: Z_d = alpha * Z_m + sqrt(1 - alpha^2) * epsilon. Here alpha describes log-weight association, not raw-weight correlation. This preserves the lognormal distribution when reproducing mothers have the specified latent normal distribution; reproductive selection can change it across generations.

Usage

het_fert(cv, alpha)

Arguments

cv

Finite nonnegative scalar coefficient of variation. Zero means fresh weights are one, with no random draw.

alpha

Finite scalar in [0,1]. Zero gives independent daughters; one copies maternal weights exactly. At zero CV the log-space formula gives W_d = W_m^alpha for supplied nonunit weights, without random innovation.

Value

A hammel_het_fert specification for set_fertility() or fertility(). Construction consumes no random draws.

Details

Simulation draws weights for all recorded women when persons has no hetfert column, or retains supplied finite strictly positive female values. An incomplete supplied column is an error. Male weights are unused; newly created male entries are NA. Draws follow the simulation seed. The output persons table always contains hetfert when this model is enabled, including zero-year runs. Enabled restarts retain weights. With hetfert = NULL, output omits the column even if supplied, so later re-enabling draws fresh weights for all women.

Examples

het_fert(cv = 0.5, alpha = 0.4)
#> $cv
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $alpha
#> [1] 0.4
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "hammel_het_fert"
